evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` (3.1 s): byte-identical to experiments/results.txt. Independent scripts /tmp/claude-0/audit-loopclosure-twin/indep.py and indep2.py (no subject import) use closed-form chi-square CDFs (F2 = 1-e^{-x/2}; F3 = erf(sqrt(x/2)) - sqrt(2x/pi) e^{-x/2}), find the optimal gate by bisection on L'(g) (not the author's closed form or golden section), and integrate the fitted-variance expectation by Simpson on Gamma(n) with a u^2 substitution plus a 200k-draw Monte Carlo. Reproduced: g_t=0.0771, radius 0.278, reject 0.0212, accept 0.0374, cost 0.0940; k=2/3 rho=1/2 exact rates 0.0212/0.3815/0.0524/0.5876 and 0.0374/0.0364/0.0055/0.0053; alpha^(1/rho^2) row 0.0000/0.0100/0.1292/0.3162/0.5995; table 3 real costs, real-opt radii 1.61/2.23/2.78/3.73/4.52/5.77/6.625, regrets 145.5/27.6/0/37.0/61.8/54.4/34.8%; ratios 2.51/4.43/6.98; c_false sweep 395.5-395.8/203.7/61.8/3.0/0; fixed-inflation rows 0.15899/0.04418/0.00772/0/0.01435/0.05257/0.12711 and 0/0.03020/0.06692/0.09876/0.15082/0.20974/0.29667; fitted regret n=2/3/5/10/30/100/1000 = 0.05371/0.03490/0.02019/0.00970/0.00313/0.00093/0.00009 and n=59 the first below 1% (58: 1.01%, 59: 0.99%). Also derived the k=2 stationarity by hand: (A/s2)e^{-g/2s2} = (B/v)e^{-g/2v} gives g = 2 s2 v/tau2 ln(Av/(Bs2)), unique interior minimum iff Av/(Bs2) > 1, otherwise g=0. Not 4: n=1 fitted regret is 0.10734 in results.txt vs 0.10788 independently (0.5% low; README/paper '67.5%' is 67.8%) because _gamma_weights truncates the Gamma density at x=1e-3 and renormalises (model.py:113; for kappa=0.5 the weights' mean is 1.033, not 1); and regret() can go negative when the true optimum is the boundary g=0: `regret(0.0, 0.04, 1.0, 0.9, 100.0)` = -0.00365 because opt_gate's grid starts at s2*e^-6 and never evaluates g=0 (model.py:73). Defects: opt_gate's log grid (model.py:73) never considers the g=0 boundary that opt_gate_k2 returns, so regret can be negative; _gamma_weights is an ad hoc midpoint rule with a hard 1e-3 floor that is biased for kappa<=1 (mean 1.033 at kappa=0.5, i.e. k=1, n=1), with no warning; star imports in __init__.py, tests and run.py; run.py also inserts src on sys.path by hand.
evidence.claims: Checked: twin gate 0.278 m / cost 0.094 / 2.1% (results.txt:2, pass); rho=2 38.2% exact vs MC 38.0% (results.txt:6, pass); 4.4x (results.txt:29, pass); regret 61.8% / 54% (results.txt:23-24, pass); alpha^(1/rho^2) 31.6% (pass); pessimistic twin 145% (pass); c_false 396%/3%/reject-all at 1000 (pass); repair 6% at n=10, <1% at n=59 (pass); '11 tests, ~1 s' and '~5 s' (pass); limits stated (README:15, paper Limitations); ARPG non-affiliation stated (README:13). Weak points: the paper calls the repair rows 'exact expectations' (whitepaper.md:3) but they are a truncated quadrature, off by 0.5% at n=1 (67.5% printed, 67.8% true); the closed-form gate is presented without saying it is the classical likelihood-ratio threshold for unequal-variance Gaussians, so a reader may take it as a contribution. Live page not verifiable.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could reuse the code as a correct, dependency-free oracle for chi-square gate costs and as a teaching example of variance mismatch. As research it is thin: the optimal gate is the Bayes / likelihood-ratio threshold between N(0,s2 I) and N(0,(s2+tau2) I) (Van Trees 1968, Part I; any detection-theory text), alpha^(1/rho^2) is one line for k=2, and the 'repair' is plug-in variance estimation whose O(1/n) regret is standard. The SLAM-side prior work a reviewer would expect is missing: loop-closure verification and robust back ends beyond Sunderhauf & Protzel (RRR, Latif, Cadena & Neira 2013; DCS, Agarwal et al. 2013; max-mixtures, Olson & Agarwal 2013; PCM, Mangelson et al. 2018) and covariance-consistency / NEES calibration of odometry (Bar-Shalom, Li & Kirubarajan 2001), which is exactly the practitioner's version of the repair. No real or simulated odometry data, so rho is a knob. Not publishable at a robotics venue as is.
evidence.domain: The chi-square gate itself is standard practice and is modelled correctly. Departures a SLAM practitioner would flag first: real loop-closure residuals live in SE(2)/SE(3) (3 or 6 dof with rotation-translation coupling), not isotropic 2-D translation; the gate in practice is a Mahalanobis test against the propagated covariance, whose scale grows with loop length, so 'twin noise too small' is a covariance-overconfidence problem usually handled by covariance inflation/calibration against NEES, not a single s; false closures from aliasing are not zero-mean Gaussian with a known tau; and modern systems use robust kernels or consistency-set selection (PCM) rather than a single hard gate. All of these are acknowledged in Limitations, not addressed.

defects.what: Tests do not guard the repair and inflation results: a wrong degrees-of-freedom in fitted_regret (n*k/2 -> n*k/2+1, halves the n=1 regret) survives because test_fit_regret_matches_simulation's delta=0.0015 is ~12% of the n=8 value; c -> c*c in gate_inflation_regret survives (only c=1 tested); the quadrature cut-off change survives; no test pins any results.txt row.

Novelty and prior work: the closed-form gate is the classical likelihood-ratio / Bayes threshold for two zero-mean Gaussians of unequal variance and the repair is plug-in variance estimation, neither attributed; SLAM loop-closure verification (RRR, DCS, max-mixtures, PCM) and odometry covariance-consistency (NEES) literature is not cited, so a reader cannot tell what, if anything, is new.

regret() can be negative: opt_gate's log grid starts at s2*e^-6 and never evaluates the g=0 boundary, so when rejecting everything is optimal (Av/(Bs2) <= 1) regret(0.0, 0.04, 1.0, 0.9, 100.0) = -0.00365. No published row uses this path, but section-5-style calls through regret() would print negative regret.

_gamma_weights truncates the Gamma density at x=1e-3 and renormalises with a midpoint rule: the n=1 repair row is 0.10734 (67.5%) vs 0.10788 (67.8%) exactly, and for kappa=0.5 (k=1, n=1) the weights' mean is 1.033; the paper calls these rows 'exact expectations'.

Domain scope: isotropic 2-D translation residual with a fixed s stands in for an SE(2)/SE(3) Mahalanobis residual whose covariance grows with loop length; false closures assumed zero-mean Gaussian with known tau; hard gate only. Acknowledged in Limitations, not modelled.
Star imports in __init__.py, tests and run.py; run.py edits sys.path by hand.

verdict: A small, clean and fully reproducible stylised study: run.py and figure.py regenerate results.txt and the SVG byte-for-byte, and independent scripts (closed-form chi-square CDFs, bisection optimum, untruncated quadrature and Monte Carlo) reproduce every number in all seven result blocks except the n=1 repair row (0.10734 printed vs 0.10788, a 0.5% quadrature truncation the paper calls 'exact'). A latent bug lets regret() go negative when the optimum is the g=0 boundary. It misses the bar on verification: 3 of 4 seeded mutants survive, including a wrong degrees-of-freedom in the repair that halves its n=1 result, because the simulation test's tolerance is ~12% and no test pins a published number. As research it restates the classical unequal-variance likelihood-ratio threshold and plug-in variance estimation without saying so, omits the loop-closure verification (RRR, DCS, PCM) and covariance-consistency literature, and uses no odometry data. Correct and finished; not yet a contribution a SLAM reviewer would accept.
